cap.untrusted: In Restricted Mode TaskKeeper only shows your tasks and runs; creating or running tasks requires a trusted workspace, because a task runs an agent on that repository.
cap.virtual: TaskKeeper needs a real Git repository on disk to create isolated worktrees.
welcome.inbox:
Nothing waiting for you.

When a scheduled task finishes, its result appears here with the diff, the tests and two buttons: accept into your branch or throw it away.

[New task](command:taskkeeper.newTask)
welcome.tasks:
No tasks yet.

A task runs Claude Code or Codex on a schedule, inside its own Git worktree, so your repository is never touched until you review.

[New task](command:taskkeeper.newTask)
[Get started (guided tour)](command:taskkeeper.getStarted)
cmd.setConcurrency: Set Concurrent Runs on This Machine
cfg.dataDir: Folder where TaskKeeper keeps its local database, worktrees and logs. Leave empty for the default (`%APPDATA%\Argalla\TaskKeeper` on Windows).
cfg.defaultTimezone: IANA time zone offered by default when creating a task (for example `Europe/Madrid`). Empty uses the system time zone.
cfg.notifications: Show a notification when a run finishes, fails or is waiting for your review.
walk.title: Get started with TaskKeeper
walk.desc: Schedule Claude Code or Codex to work while you are away. Four short steps.
walk.axes.title: Two choices, not two paths
walk.axes.desc:
Every task is a point on two independent axes.

**Conversation** — start fresh, continue an existing one, or fork it.
**Where it works** — isolated in a worktree you review, or in the conversation itself.

The panel offers the two most common combinations as shortcuts, and an **Advanced** link to mix them freely.
walk.axes.alt: A grid of Conversation by Where-it-works with one cell highlighted.
walk.create.title: Create your first task
walk.create.desc:
Open the panel and pick a shortcut. Choose **In a conversation** and the folder is detected from the conversation id — you do not have to find it.

[Create a task](command:taskkeeper.newTask)
walk.create.alt: The task panel with two shortcut cards and a highlighted field.
walk.schedule.title: Say when it runs
walk.schedule.desc:
Every day, some weekdays, or once. Add several times — for example **15:00** and **20:00** — and the panel shows the next runs live.

Missed the time because the machine was off? Choose whether to skip, run late, or wait for you.
walk.schedule.alt: A clock and two scheduled time chips.
walk.results.title: See the result
walk.results.desc: A finished run opens as a readable transcript, with a one-line summary. An isolated task also shows the diff and tests, with **Accept into branch** or **Reject**. A task in a conversation adds its turns to the chat and keeps the log for you to review.
walk.results.alt: A conversation transcript beside a diff with accept and reject buttons.
